guard: A hosted drive's own journal reads share one replay durable per takeover. Reads under one takeover id run one at a time in the process, so a parallel of three asks answered within one second fails no branch while RunHost.status reads the same id; a step read or the no-record diagnostic that loses a round to another reader replays again, at most three times, and raises the race after the third; any other failure is raised on the first read.
proveWith: pnpm mutation-proof --config implementations/runtime/smoke/mutations/run-host-replay.json   # --config resolves against the repo root, never the cwd
why: Issue #1623 asked for a runtime cell where a parallel of three asks settling within the same second fails no branch, with the shared-durable behaviour as its mutant, and for the race to be retried at the step the way activateRun retries it.

The shared-durable mutant (RH7) reverts the per-durable serialisation in packages/core/src/run-journal.ts. The suite loads @cotal-ai/core from dist, so that mutation and its control build core first and rebuild it after the restore. RH8 is the positive control for that build path: it disables the freshness guard in the same file and must redden a cell of its own.

RH7 is killed only because block 1 also reads the drive's takeover id through RunHost.status on the driver's connection. Without that reader the three asks' step reads all go through one RunScopeAuthority, whose own promise chain already puts them in order, so reverting the core lock alone leaves a hosted parallel green. The authority's chain is therefore not registered as a mutant; see `redundant`.

RH1 to RH6 mutate the runtime sources the suite imports through relative paths, so no build sits between them and the run. RH5 and RH6 swap each call site back to the unretried core replay under the same local name, which is the source as it was before this change.

mutations.name: RH1: a step read raises the race on its first lost round again
mutations.find: if (!(e instanceof RunJournalReplayRaced) || attempt >= OWN_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS) throw e;
mutations.expectRed: no branch fails when one of the drive's step reads loses a round to another reader
mutations.cell: no branch fails when one of the drive's step reads loses a round to another reader

mutations.name: RH2: the replay bound grows by one round
mutations.expectRed: a step read that loses every round fails with the race after three replays, not a fourth
mutations.cell: a step read that loses every round fails with the race after three replays, not a fourth

mutations.name: RH3: the replay bound shrinks by one round
mutations.expectRed: a step read that loses two rounds replays a third time and reads the run
mutations.cell: a step read that loses two rounds replays a third time and reads the run

mutations.name: RH4: every failure of a step read is replayed, not only the race
mutations.find: if (!(e instanceof RunJournalReplayRaced) || attempt >= OWN_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS) throw e;
mutations.expectRed: a step read that fails for any other reason raises that failure without replaying again
mutations.cell: a step read that fails for any other reason raises that failure without replaying again

mutations.name: RH5: the step reads go back to the unretried replay
mutations.expectRed: no branch fails when one of the drive's step reads loses a round to another reader
mutations.cell: no branch fails when one of the drive's step reads loses a round to another reader

mutations.name: RH6: the no-record diagnostic goes back to the unretried replay
mutations.replace:
import { RunJournalStore } from "./journal-store.js";
import { replayRunJournal as replayOwnJournal } from "@cotal-ai/core";
mutations.expectRed: and it still releases the run naming a journal that was activated and never pinned
mutations.cell: and it still releases the run naming a journal that was activated and never pinned

mutations.name: RH7: replays under one takeover id run concurrently again, sharing one durable
mutations.find: const mine = ahead === undefined ? body() : ahead.then(body);
mutations.expectRed: no branch fails while status reads the drive's own takeover id
mutations.cell: no branch fails while status reads the drive's own takeover id

mutations.name: RH8: CONTROL (expect KILLED): the freshness guard stops refusing, so a tail is read as the run
mutations.expectRed: a step read that loses every round fails with the race after three replays, not a fourth
mutations.cell: a step read that loses every round fails with the race after three replays, not a fourth
mutations.note: Proves the suite reads the rebuilt core rather than a stale dist, so RH7's verdict is about the lock and not about module resolution.

redundant.name: the authority's own read chain is removed
redundant.why: SURVIVED three runs of three, each paired in the same run with RH5 (same file) as its control, which was KILLED every time. With the core per-durable lock in place, every read the authority makes already waits for the previous read of the same durable, so dropping the authority's own chain changes no order a cell can see. It becomes observable only with RH7 applied too: with both edits and core rebuilt, three runs of three failed both panels before any ask parked and before any status read was made, with block 1's branches recording L4000 `consumer deleted` (two runs) or an incomplete replay (one run). That is two mutations, not one, so it is recorded here rather than registered.
